newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi Arabia seeks 1.72 mln T feed barley - trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia seeks 1.72 mln T feed barley - trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabia will tender on September 20 to import a total of 1.72 million tonnes of optional-origin feed barley for delivery in October, November and December, European grain traders said on Wednesday.
Details of tonnages and delivery dates are as follows -

Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest importer of feed barley, recently bought some 800,000 tonnes of feed barley from the world market, with the lion's share - at least 600,000 tonnes- going to the European Union.
The transaction was made at $160 to $162 per tonne, including cost, freight and insurance. Substracting freight costs the equivalent Fob price for the purchase stood around $142-145 per tonne.
Exporters said the Saudis were back because they wanted to take advantage of declining world prices. World barley is currently worth some $130 per tonne, Fob.
One trader also linked the tender to budgetary arbitrages in Saudi Arabia.
"They are buying to clean out their budget allocations expiring on December 31." he said.
The tender calls for deliveries until end December - although this is bound to pose logistical problems - only because they qualify for 1996 funds, he said.
With the new tender Saudi Arabia may have covered its import requirements until April, traders said.

In its latest report the International Grains Council said Saudi Arabia might import 3.5 million tonnes of barley in 1996/97 against an estimated 3.2 million tonnes in 1995. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
